title: InertiaMPDD: Multimodal Personalized Depression Detection via Emotional Inertia-Inspired Dynamics Modeling
abstract: arXiv:2611.16647v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Multimodal depression screening estimates risk from speech, visual behavior and language. Current methods mainly predict labels, with limited evidence of departures from a non-depressed reference. Recording-level supervision also leaves fine-grained emotional dynamics unannotated. Motivated by emotional inertia, the persistence of affect, InertiaMPDD learns healthy next-state patterns using a world-model-inspired latent predictor. Using pretrained multimodal representations, it predicts from observed history and context. Reference deviation, residual decay rate and a Jacobian spectral descriptor form reference-derived emotional dynamics descriptors, evaluated as candidate proxy biomarkers for standalone screening and personalized decision correction. Across five cohorts from four datasets, fusion reaches 98.41% F1 on D-Vlog and 84.98% on LMVD. Standalone descriptors outperform fixed additive fusion on MPDD but discriminate weakly on AVEC

translated_title: InertiaMPDD：基于情绪惯性启发的动态建模的多模态个性化抑郁症检测
translated_abstract: 多模态抑郁症筛查通过语音、视觉行为和语言来估计风险。现有方法主要局限于预测标签，缺乏相对于非抑郁参照状态发生偏离的证据。此外，录音级别的监督方式也使得细粒度的情绪动态未被标注。受情绪惯性（即情感的持续性）启发，InertiaMPDD使用受世界模型启发的潜在预测器来学习健康的下一状态模式。该方法利用预训练的多模态表示，从观测历史和上下文信息中进行预测。参照偏离、残差衰减率和雅可比谱描述符构成了基于参照衍生的情绪动力学描述符，这些描述符被评估为用于独立筛查和个性化决策校正的候选代理生物标志物。在来自四个数据集的五个队列上，融合方法在D-Vlog上达到98.41%的F1分数，在LMVD上达到84.98%。独立的描述符在MPDD上优于固定加性融合方法，但在AVEC上判别能力较弱。
tldr: 受情绪惯性概念启发，该论文提出InertiaMPDD方法，通过世界模型式潜在预测器学习健康情绪状态转移模式，并以参照偏离、残差衰减率和雅可比谱描述符等情绪动力学描述符作为代理生物标志物，实现多模态个性化抑郁症检测，在多个数据集上取得优异性能。
en_tdlr: Inspired by emotional inertia, this paper proposes InertiaMPDD, which learns healthy next-state patterns via a world-model-inspired latent predictor and derives emotional dynamics descriptors (reference deviation, residual decay rate, and Jacobian spectral descriptor) as proxy biomarkers for multimodal personalized depression detection, achieving strong performance across multiple datasets.
